key_insight: A unified AI pipeline segments hair and estimates skin and hair characteristics from macroscopic dermatological images to support future laser treatment parameterization.
clinical_relevance: Objective measurements could help reduce reliance on subjective assessment, but automated treatment settings and clinical benefits remain unvalidated.
method: Custom-trained YOLOv9 variant for hair instance segmentation.
Classical image processing to estimate phototype, hair density, color, and thickness.
Spectrophotometric color calibration to account for illumination differences.
evidence_signal: On a custom dataset featuring short, shaved hairs typical of pre-treatment images, segmentation achieved mAP@50 of approximately 0.80.
watch_item: Generalizability across skin tones, imaging conditions, and clinical settings is not established by the abstract.
paper_title: Hair Segmentation and Skin Characterization on Macroscopic Dermatological Images for Laser Treatment Parameterization
